component_fit_evidence: HubSpot lifecycle-stage guidance defines stage properties and marketing/sales handoffs; Salesforce Trailhead/Journey Builder add platform workflow context. These are useful system examples but not a platform-neutral CRM operating model or complete service, sales and retention framework.
material_gaps: Business-model-specific lifecycle definitions, customer value, cross-functional ownership, contact governance, Indonesia operating examples and CRM economics are not comprehensively covered by broad academy portals.
next_action: Build B2C, subscription and B2B lifecycle maps with stage entry/exit, event, owner, service/sales handoff, KPI and contact policy. Separate generic CRM strategy from platform-specific properties.

component_fit_evidence: Salesforce Contact Builder, Data Extensions and Data Designer document contact records, related data, sources and cross-channel activation. UU PDP 27/2022 provides the Indonesian processing framework. These are useful primary references but Salesforce architecture is not a neutral customer data model.
material_gaps: Identity resolution, deterministic/probabilistic match, survivorship, merge/split, purpose/legal-basis records, retention/deletion and access controls across systems need vendor-neutral design and local privacy review.
next_action: Create ERD/data dictionary for account, person/contact, transaction, product, event, source, purpose/legal basis, channel preference, consent history and retention. Include false-match, correction, deletion and audit scenarios.

component_fit_evidence: HubSpot lifecycle-stage guidance supports stage categorisation and lead handoff; Salesforce Contact Builder/Data Extensions support operational audience data structures. The mapped course portals are useful entry routes, but do not evidence a calibrated lead-scoring methodology.
material_gaps: Score calibration against qualified pipeline/downstream revenue, exclusions/decay, sample size, false positives, data quality, privacy and refresh cadence need worked datasets. Email opens are weak intent proxies under privacy protections.
next_action: Create a six-segment taxonomy and lead-score model; split fit from intent, define exclusions/decay and test against held-out sales outcomes. Require consent/data-quality checks before activation.

component_fit_evidence: HubSpot workflow enrollment and Salesforce Journey Builder goal/exit guidance support event- or condition-driven automation. WhatsApp Business Policy provides current message-permission and template boundaries. These sources are relevant but use different platform concepts and do not fully cover cross-channel orchestration.
material_gaps: Event schema/integration, deduplication, suppression precedence, quiet hours, cross-channel frequency, service-vs-marketing rules, retries and consent changes need a cross-platform operating example.
next_action: Build welcome/cart/post-purchase/win-back workflows with purchase/opt-out suppression, eligibility, delays, frequency caps, exception paths and QA cases. Verify event source and destination state.

component_fit_evidence: WhatsApp policy specifies approved templates for business-initiated messages and the 24-hour customer-service window; Gmail documents sender authentication and bulk-sender requirements; RFC 8058 defines one-click unsubscribe signalling; UU PDP adds Indonesian privacy context. Coverage is strongest for email/WhatsApp, not all four channels.
material_gaps: SMS and push provider-specific permission, pricing, opt-out and delivery rules; WhatsApp opt-in categories/template costs; Gmail volume thresholds; transactional-vs-marketing distinction and Indonesian legal basis need separate checks.
next_action: Create a channel matrix differentiating email, WhatsApp, SMS and push by purpose, permission, SLA, format, pricing, service window, opt-out and fallback. Separate service and promotional examples; phone number does not imply marketing permission.

component_fit_evidence: HubSpot enrollment and Salesforce Journey Builder goals/exit provide workflow mechanics. Google Cloud retry guidance distinguishes transient/permanent errors and safe retries; Consent Mode explains tag-state propagation. These are helpful product docs, not a complete integration engineering standard.
material_gaps: Idempotency keys, webhook authentication, retry/backoff, dead-letter queues, event ordering, API limits, schema evolution, monitoring, reconciliation and manual replay need a practical integration lab. Consent Mode does not collect or persist consent.
next_action: Build form-to-CRM-to-message flow with signed webhook, idempotency key, bounded retry/backoff, duplicate event, missing field, consent withdrawal, error queue, alert and manual replay tests.

component_fit_evidence: Gmail sender guidance provides authentication, spam-rate and bulk-sender requirements; RFC 8058 specifies one-click unsubscribe headers; UU PDP and Google Consent Mode clarify privacy/tag boundaries. These sources support deliverability/compliance fundamentals but not an entire personalisation governance model.
material_gaps: Data minimisation, purpose limitation, preference centre, frequency fatigue, dynamic-content fallback, provider-level diagnostics and open-rate privacy limitations require further platform and local legal review.
next_action: Build a personalisation inventory with field, source, purpose, necessity, expiry, fallback, suppression and preference. Add SPF/DKIM/DMARC, bounce/complaint, unsubscribe and test-send evidence; caveat open-rate reporting.

chapter_title: Retention, Churn, Cohort & Customer Lifetime Value
component_fit_evidence: GA4 cohort exploration provides an official example of defining inclusion and return criteria; HubSpot lifecycle stages supports operational stage tracking. These do not establish universal retention definitions or finance-approved contribution LTV.
material_gaps: Churn by business model, cohort event/time grain, censoring, contribution margin, refunds, discounts, service cost, acquisition cost and horizon need finance-approved definitions and worked cases. Revenue-only LTV is not contribution LTV.
next_action: Build a synthetic cohort workbook with acquisition cohort, eligible base, return event, retention, churn, gross margin, refunds/discounts, variable service cost and LTV sensitivity; validate assumptions with finance SME.

component_fit_evidence: Salesforce Journey Builder goals provide outcome tracking and possible exit behaviour; HubSpot workflow controls help define eligible contacts. Messaging-provider policy and deliverability references provide guardrails. None of these product-operation documents is a complete causal experimentation method.
material_gaps: Randomisation unit, persistent holdout, journey/channel contamination, sample size/power, primary metric, guardrails, multiple comparisons, seasonality and incremental margin require a statistical method and worked calculation.
next_action: Specify a persistent randomised holdout with eligibility, assignment persistence, baseline, sample-size assumptions, primary outcome, guardrails and stopping rules. Reconcile at customer level and measure incremental contribution, not only attributed opens/clicks.

component_fit_evidence: Salesforce Contact Builder/Data Extensions, HubSpot lifecycle/workflow guidance, UU PDP, WhatsApp policy, Gmail sender rules and GA4 cohort documentation jointly support major capstone components. They are a source set, not an integrated validated CRM solution.
material_gaps: End-to-end customer data-to-journey, consent ledger, channel pricing, deliverability, suppression, failure recovery, cohort economics, holdout and a complete reference solution/rubric are still missing. Local legal interpretation requires counsel.
next_action: Deliver one SIMULATED case from ERD through segment, lawful-processing analysis, channel choice, automation/failure tests, message samples, deliverability checks, cohort/LTV and holdout evaluation; require independent CRM, privacy and measurement review.
